citation.title: Topology optimization using artificial intelligence
citation.authors: Ahmed Ait Ouchaoui, Mohammed Nassraoui, Bouchaib Radi
citation.venue: Incertitudes et fiabilité des systèmes multiphysiques (ISTE OpenScience), vol. 8, no. 2, pp. 38-42 (per the PDF file name and page footers; diamond open access per OpenAlex)
citation.version_coded: Version of record, publisher PDF (5 pages) from openscience.fr (the open copy OpenAlex lists), read in full as text; pages 40-41 (Figs. 2-3, Table 1) also checked on the rendered pages. The adjudicator re-read the same PDF (openscience.fr/IMG/pdf/iste_incertfia24v8n2_7.pdf) in full on 2026-09-24, including the rendered pages 40-41

included.reason: I-QUALITY (screened I-SPEED; no TopologyGAN run time is reported anywhere, and the only quantitative ML-vs-classical comparison is structural quality against SIMP, Table 1; §5.1 rule 2)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Cantilever (120x60 elements, volume fraction 0.4): against the SIMP design, the TopologyGAN design has 2.72x the peak von Mises stress, 5.62x the peak displacement and 8.08x the deformation energy.
claim.key_phrase: provides considerable benefits in terms of improved design correctness and computing performance
claim.location: Sec. 3, Table 1 and the paragraph after Fig. 3 (p. 41): the first quantitative comparison with a classical method. The abstract and conclusion compare only qualitatively (the key phrase is from the abstract)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not derivable: SIMP took 54 s for 33 iterations on an Intel Core i7-8565U computer with 16 GB RAM (Sec. 3, p. 41), but no TopologyGAN time, hardware or training cost is reported. The abstract and conclusion still claim better computing performance.
claim.alternatives: (1) Abstract, qualitative: TopologyGAN brings considerable benefits in design correctness and computing performance over SIMP; this contradicts Table 1. (2) Conclusion, qualitative: TopologyGAN promises optimal designs with better accuracy and lower computational cost. (3) Sec. 3: weight reduction vs the original solid design is 46% for TopologyGAN and 40% for SIMP.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP compliance minimization, volume fraction 0.4, penalization 3 (Sec. 2, Eq. 1; Sec. 3)
baseline.implementation: not stated (the static-analysis outputs suggest a commercial FE package [inferred])
baseline.hardware_classical: ASUS computer, Intel Core i7-8565U CPU at 1.80 GHz (a laptop-class CPU [inferred]), 16 GB RAM (Sec. 3, p. 41)
baseline.problem_size: Cantilever 120 x 60 mm, 1 mm elements, 7200 elements; inclined tip load Fx = 0.5 N, Fy = 0.87 N (Sec. 2, p. 40; units checked on the rendered page) [2D inferred]
baseline.classical_iterations: 33 iterations (Sec. 3, p. 41); stopping rule not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; TopologyGAN (Nie et al. 2021) is trained on SIMP ground truth per Sec. 2, but whether a published model was used or the authors retrained it is not stated
baseline.quality_metric: Static analysis of each design: peak von Mises stress, peak displacement in Y and deformation energy (Table 1) [FE re-analysis inferred]; weight reduction relative to the solid design
baseline.quality_gap: TopologyGAN vs SIMP: peak stress 0.809 vs 0.297 MPa (2.72x); peak displacement 51.097 vs 9.09 x1e-5 mm (5.62x); deformation energy 41.79 vs 5.17 x1e-7 mJ (8.08x) (Table 1; Sec. 3). Weight reduction 46% vs 40%, so volumes differ

R1.evidence: Sec. 3, Table 1: one TopologyGAN design is compared with one SIMP design, but the volumes differ (weight reduction 46% vs 40%, i.e. 54% vs 60% of the solid weight [derived]), although both nominally target volume fraction 0.4. How the TopologyGAN design was produced (pretrained or retrained model, input resolution, post-processing) is not stated, and the SIMP stopping rule is not given. Quality is reported, but matching is loose.

R2.evidence: Stratum Q: only the SIMP time (54 s) is reported; with no TopologyGAN time there is no speed comparison, so criteria (a)-(e) do not apply. Under the §11 stratum-Q rule (2026-09-24) only criterion (b) could apply, and the abstract (p. 38) gives no baseline figures, so (b) is not observed.

R3.evidence: No quantified speed claim. The abstract and conclusion assert better computing performance without any time; for C3, no training or data-generation cost is mentioned.

R4.evidence: Table 1 (p. 41): both returned designs are scored by the same static analysis (peak stress, displacement, deformation energy) [FE re-analysis inferred; the tool is not named], on the smoothed geometries of Fig. 3, whose post-processing is not described. The reported weight reductions (40% SIMP, 46% TopologyGAN, p. 41) leave 60% and 54% of the solid plate of Fig. 2 (p. 40) [derived], against vf = 0.4 (p. 40); this violation is not acknowledged, and failed designs are neither defined nor counted.

notes: Screening code was I-SPEED; full text gives stratum Q because TopologyGAN is never timed. The abstract and conclusion claim that TopologyGAN beats SIMP on design correctness and computing performance, but the article's own Table 1 shows the TopologyGAN design is worse on all three metrics (2.72x stress, 5.62x displacement, 8.08x deformation energy; ratios stated in Sec. 3 and re-derived from Table 1). This claim-versus-evidence mismatch matters for C4. The article is a short comparison of an existing method (TopologyGAN, Nie et al. 2021) with SIMP on one case, not a new method; it is kept as an include because it makes an explicit ML-vs-classical claim, but a verifier could weigh FT-TYPE (benchmark-only). Internal inconsistencies: the volume fraction is 0.4 (Sec. 2), yet the weight reductions are 40% (SIMP) and 46% (TopologyGAN), which would fit a volume fraction near 0.6 or 0.54 [inferred]; two figures are numbered Figure 2; the conclusion says SIMP increases stress, displacement and energy, which is relative to the original solid design, not to TopologyGAN. Table 1 values and the load units (N) were checked on the rendered pages 40-41. TopologyGAN's training data and whether its trained weights came from Nie et al. are not stated, so ood_test = unclear. No code or data statement. retest_candidate false: no code from this article, no ML time and no speed claim to re-test. No author named Jun Wang.

R1.reason: In stratum Q, R1 applies as written (§11), and none of the §5.3 fail markers holds: no TopologyGAN time is reported to set against the SIMP run, and a quality comparison does exist (Table 1, p. 41). The abstract-versus-data contradiction the second coder cites is a C4 matter. What remains is loose matching: volumes differ (40% vs 46% weight reduction), and the SIMP stopping rule is unstated.

R4.reason: Both designs are scored by one static analysis (Table 1, p. 41; FE inferred), but the reported weight reductions leave 60% and 54% of the solid plate against vf = 0.4 (pp. 40-41) [derived], unacknowledged, and no failure criterion is given. Unlike a problem where no failure mode can occur, a volume constraint applies here, so this is the §5.3 R4 partial case.
